files_summary.pg_schema.json: Postgres schema dump: schemas (list) + tables (dict of {schema: {table: {columns, rows}}}). Columns carry name/type/pk/fk. Tools build an in-memory SQLite DB from this and run real SQL. Schemas: public (customers, orders, products, order_items, support_tickets), analytics (daily_revenue, product_views, funnel_events), reporting (monthly_kpis, top_products, segment_summary).
files_summary.README.md: Schema, lifecycles and business rules of this benchmark's datastore.

tool_schemas.name: list_schemas
tool_schemas.description: Returns a paginated list of schemas available in this LedgerSight Commerce Analytics Hub database. It refuses requests with an invalid or expired cursor, or a non-positive/invalid limit, because it cannot page results safely. It also refuses requests from callers that are not authorized to enumerate database metadata.

limit.description: Maximum number of schemas to return

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor for fetching the next page of results

tool_schemas.name: list_objects
tool_schemas.description: Returns the objects in the requested schema, optionally filtered by object type (table, view, sequence, or extension). It refuses requests when schema_name is missing, empty, or does not exist, because there is no schema to inspect. It also refuses requests with an unsupported object_type or from callers without permission to view objects in that schema.

tool_schemas.name: get_object_details
tool_schemas.description: Returns detailed metadata for a single database object (such as its columns/definition where applicable) within the given schema and object type. It refuses requests when schema_name or object_name is missing/empty, when the schema or object cannot be found, or when the object_type does not match the actual object, because the target is ambiguous or invalid. It also refuses requests from callers who are not permitted to view metadata for that object.

tool_schemas.name: explain_query
tool_schemas.description: Returns the database execution plan for the provided SQL, and when analyze=true it runs the statement to include actual execution statistics. It refuses requests with empty or invalid SQL, SQL that cannot be planned, or statements that would execute unsafe or unauthorized operations when analyze=true, because it must be able to plan (and optionally run) the query safely. It also refuses hypothetical_indexes entries that are missing required fields (table/columns), reference non-existent tables/columns, or specify an unsupported index method.

analyze.description: When True, actually runs the query to show real execution statistics instead of estimates. Takes longer but provides more accurate information.
analyze.title: Analyze

hypothetical_indexes.description:
A list of hypothetical indexes to simulate. Each index must be a dictionary with these keys:
    - 'table': The table name to add the index to (e.g., 'users')
    - 'columns': List of column names to include in the index (e.g., ['email'] or ['last_name', 'first_name'])
    - 'using': Optional index method (default: 'btree', other options include 'hash', 'gist', etc.)

Examples: [
    {"table": "users", "columns": ["email"], "using": "btree"},
    {"table": "orders", "columns": ["user_id", "created_at"]}
]
If there is no hypothetical index, you can pass an empty list.
hypothetical_indexes.title: Hypothetical Indexes

tool_schemas.name: analyze_workload_indexes
tool_schemas.description: Analyzes observed query workload and returns recommended indexes within the requested size constraints using the selected method. It refuses requests with an unsupported method or an invalid max_index_size_mb (non-integer or non-positive), because it cannot produce bounded recommendations. It also refuses requests when workload statistics are unavailable (for example, required monitoring extensions are not enabled) or the caller lacks permission to read performance metadata.

tool_schemas.name: analyze_query_indexes
tool_schemas.description: Analyzes the provided list of SQL queries (up to 10) and returns index recommendations bounded by max_index_size_mb using the selected method. It refuses requests when queries is missing, empty, contains more than 10 entries, or includes empty/invalid SQL, because it cannot analyze an unbounded or non-parsable workload. It also refuses requests with an unsupported method, an invalid max_index_size_mb, or queries the caller is not allowed to analyze against the underlying schema objects.

queries.description: List of Query strings to analyze
queries.title: Queries

tool_schemas.name: analyze_db_health
tool_schemas.description:
Analyzes database health. Here are the available health checks:
- index - checks for invalid, duplicate, and bloated indexes
- connection - checks the number of connection and their utilization
- vacuum - checks vacuum health for transaction id wraparound
- sequence - checks sequences at risk of exceeding their maximum value
- replication - checks replication health including lag and slots
- buffer - checks for buffer cache hit rates for indexes and tables
- constraint - checks for invalid constraints
- all - runs all checks
You can optionally specify a single health check or a comma-separated list of health checks. The default is 'all' checks.

health_type.description: Optional. Valid values are: all, buffer, connection, constraint, index, replication, sequence, vacuum.
health_type.title: Health Type

tool_schemas.name: get_top_queries
tool_schemas.description: Returns a ranked list of the slowest or most resource-intensive queries based on pg_stat_statements data, using the requested sort and limit. It refuses requests with an invalid limit (non-integer or non-positive) or an unsupported sort_by value, because it cannot rank results consistently. It also refuses requests when pg_stat_statements data is unavailable or the caller lacks permission to read query statistics.

limit.description: Number of queries to return when ranking based on mean_time or total_time
limit.title: Limit

sort_by.description: Ranking criteria: 'total_time' for total execution time or 'mean_time' for mean execution time per call, or 'resources' for resource-intensive queries
sort_by.title: Sort By

tool_schemas.name: execute_sql
tool_schemas.description: Executes the provided SQL statement and returns the resulting rows for queries that produce a result set, along with execution status for other statements. It refuses requests with missing/empty SQL, SQL that fails validation or parsing, or statements the caller is not authorized to run. It also refuses operations that are blocked by the service’s safety and policy controls (for example, attempting to access restricted schemas or perform prohibited administrative actions).

metadata.name: LedgerSight Commerce Analytics Hub
metadata.description: A backend service that stores commerce datasets and derived reporting tables, and provides SQL execution plus automated query, index, and database health analytics for reporting and performance optimization.
